meta.bit_reading_note: Part A positions (part W) run the wait test on the label's chain: classical bits c0 to c4 are the end lines' results, in the order L1, L3, L1, L3, L1 (manacitra.wait.WAIT_TEST_ROUNDS), and c5 is M's; Part B (part B): classical bit i is the i-th qubit of the label's qubits
meta.description: Kickoff 48, the wait test on hardware. Part A: the wait test (manacitra.wait.build_wait_test) on five chains L1-M-L3, 144-143-142, 143-144-145, 141-142-143, 132-131-138 and 125-124-123, each without and with XY4 refocusing pulses, 4 interleaved copies of 5000 shots. Part B: Ramsey and echo (manacitra.wait.part_b) on Kickoff 47's groups, {143, 131, 124} and {142, 144, 125}, at eight waits from 0 to 4000 dt (0 to 16 us), the circuit's own wait T_M among them, each circuit twice, 2000 shots each. 104 circuits in one job, the two parts interleaved; the sampler's own dynamical decoupling and twirling off, as IBM recorded them.
meta.bit_order: Qiskit bitstrings, rightmost character = classical bit 0

built_from.how: every circuit built by manacitra.wait at this commit, unedited: Part A by build_wait_test(chain, refocus, backend), translated at optimization level 0 with the chain as the layout, XY4 by refocused; Part B by part_b and to_backend; against the live ibm_fez target at build (dt 4 ns, granularity 1)
built_from.rebuild: manacitra.wait at this commit rebuilds every circuit from the chains, groups and waits here; tests/test_wait.py rebuilds them for the offline ibm_fez snapshot and checks their structure against cells, part_B_circuits and offline_build

T_M.definition: end of M's first H (its first sx) to the start of its last H (its last sx), scheduled without refocusing

offline_build.what: the dry run before the go: the same circuits built for qiskit-ibm-runtime's offline ibm_fez snapshot, whose durations differ from the live target's (measure plus reset 786 dt, against 836 live), so its T_M, waits and refocusing pulses differ; not sent

fixed_before_the_data.rule: H48: F_pred = F_ref x (1 - dP_R(T_M)), dP_R(T_M) = P_R(T_M) - P_R(0) on M, the Ramsey P(1) pooled over Part B's two copies; d_M = F_no - F_pred, its 90% interval from a joint bootstrap of both parts. DISAGREE if any chain's d_M interval lies entirely outside [-margin, +margin]; AGREE if every chain's lies entirely inside; NOT SETTLED otherwise. A chain is informative if its dP_R(T_M) interval lies entirely above the informative floor; with none, the verdict carries ', uninformative'
fixed_before_the_data.F_classes: LOW if the 90% interval lies entirely below 0.3, HIGH if entirely above 0.6, MIDDLE otherwise
fixed_before_the_data.part_b_rule: manacitra.wait.part_b_losses at the reference wait, with its default thresholds (Kickoff 47's rule)
fixed_before_the_data.bootstraps: Part A: copies with replacement within each cell, each redrawn from a multinomial (seed bootstrap_A); Part B: manacitra.wait.part_b_losses (seed bootstrap_B); the prediction: both parts jointly, in a fixed order, chains in meta.chains order, for each F_no then F_ref (Part A's draw), then P_R(T_M) and P_R(0) (Part B's draw) (seed joint)
